extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH R01 grant applications (University of Toledo applicants / academic investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for preparing and formatting an NIH R01 application, covering FOA selection, deadlines, required attachments (Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Biosketch), human/animal subject sections, budget rules, and other required documents. Intended to ensure compliance with NIH and FOA-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the MOST RECENT funding announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should use the MOST RECENT funding announcement. Please check the “Release/Posted Date” in the “Key Dates” section of the RFA/PA to ensure that it is up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual FOAs may contain specific instructions that differ from general NIH instructions; when they do, FOA instructions take precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA-specific instructions take precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: NOTE: Individual FOAs may contain specific instructions about content, format, or length that differ from the general instructions provided by the NIH on its website and in the SF424 (R&R). In these instances, individual FOA instructions take precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check the Application and Submission Information section and Part 2 of the FOA for detailed instructions and any deviations from generic NIH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine clinical trial/participant category of FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to the parent announcements appropriate to your application (e.g., Clinical Trial Not Allowed: PA-20-185; Clinical Trial Required: PA-20-183; Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required: PA-20-184).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct parent announcement and follow its specific requirements (e.g., whether clinical trials or basic experimental studies with humans are allowed/required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and follow correct due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the actual funding announcement to see if standard due dates apply (sometimes dates vary). R01 Standard Due Dates: Cycle 1: Feb 5 (AIDS: May 7); Cycle 2: June 5 (AIDS: Sept 7); Cycle 3: Oct 5 (AIDS: Jan 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note Scientific Merit Review, Advisory Council Review, and Earliest Project Start Date windows listed in the FOA; these vary by cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI policy and Leadership Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Check your announcement to see if single or multiple Principal Investigators (PIs) are allowed. For applications designating multiple PDs/PIs, a Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH multi-PD/PI FAQ for details (link provided). Follow FOA guidance if it restricts PD/PI arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: R01 Purpose: suitable project scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Project (R01) grant is an award made to support a discrete, specified, circumscribed project to be performed by the named investigator(s) in an area representing the investigator's specific interest and competencies, based on the mission of the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposed work fits the R01 model (focused, investigator-driven project) and aligns with the NIH mission cited in the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: duration and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs appropriate for the project and a project duration of up to five years may be requested. The size and duration of each award will vary; R01s can be limited in a specific FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Part 2, Section 2. Award Budget of the FOA for any budgetary limits. Follow NIH and FOA-specific instructions for budget justification and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NIH for applications requesting ≥ $500,000 direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants requesting $500,000 or more in direct costs in any year (excluding consortium F&A) must contact NIH program staff at least 6 weeks before submitting the application and follow the Policy on the Acceptance for Review of Unsolicited Applications that Request $500,000 or More in Direct Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide and the NIH Grants Policy Statement for procedures. Individual FOAs may require additional budget information; review the FOA's Application and Submission Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Title: Limited to 200 characters (includes spaces and punctuation marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary (Abstract) format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary (Abstract): No longer than 30 lines of text. Succinct and accurate description of the proposed work, able to stand on its own (separate from the application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be informative to other persons working in the same or related fields and understandable to a scientifically literate reader. Avoid descriptions of past accomplishments and the use of the first person. State the application's broad, long-term objectives and specific aims, reference health relatedness, and describe the research design and methods. Do not include proprietary/confidential information or trade secrets. Note: the Project Summary/Abstract attachment is not the same as the Research Strategy attachment. If funded, this will be public and entered into NIH RePORT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative content and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative: No more than 3 sentences. Describe the relevance to public health: how, in the short or long term, the research would contribute to fundamental knowledge and/or application to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce illness and disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funded, this public health relevance statement will be combined with the project summary and become public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the sample format on the Biographical Sketch Format Page. Each biosketch is limited to 5 pages, including the table at the top of the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should begin with baccalaureate information. Personal Statement: briefly describe why your experience/qualifications make you well-suited for the role. You may cite up to four publications or research products (with specific rules for interim products). If citing NIH-funded studies under Public Access Policy, provide NIHMS or PMCID numbers or state 'PMC Journal – In Process' where appropriate. You may provide a URL to a full list of published work hosted on a .gov website (My Bibliography recommended). For applications due on/after Jan 25, 2022, follow updated NIH instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support section rules in Biosketch
rubrics_metrics.description: List selected ongoing and completed (during the last three years) research projects (Federal or non-Federal support). Begin with projects most relevant to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly indicate the overall goals of the projects and your overall responsibilities. Do not include number of person months or direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims: 1-page limit. The Specific Aims do NOT count toward your Research Strategy, which has its own page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conciseness: state the goals of the proposed research, summarize expected outcomes including impact, and succinctly list objectives (e.g., to test a hypothesis, create a novel design, solve a specific problem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy page limit and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy: Cannot exceed 12 pages (for R01s). This section includes three headings: Significance, Innovation, and Approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH Research Strategy structure strictly and allocate page space appropriately among the three headings. See NIH Table of Page Limits for other mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (Research Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress in the field that the proposed project addresses. Explain how the proposed project will improve scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice in one or more broad fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field will be changed if the proposed aims are achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (Research Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation or intervention(s) to be developed or used, advantages over existing methods/instrumentation/interventions, and any refinements, improvements, or new applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (Research Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses to be used to accomplish the specific aims of the project. Include Preliminary Studies/Progress Report in the Approach section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include how data will be collected, analyzed, and interpreted and any resource sharing plans as appropriate. Discuss potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success. If the project is in early stages, describe strategy to establish feasibility and management of high-risk aspects. Point out any hazardous procedures/situations/materials and precautions to be exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Letter suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover Letter: NIH suggests that you request a specific Institute/Center and a specific review committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with the project officer listed on the funding announcement for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs must identify facilities used, their capacities, pertinent capabilities, relative proximity and extent of availability to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the scientific environment in which the research will be conducted contributes to the probability of success. For Early Stage Investigators, describe institutional investment in the investigator's success (refer to NIH Early Stage Investigator Policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography/References Cited page-count rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography/References Cited — this section does not count toward your page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete references here; it will not reduce your Research Strategy page allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects sections and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Subjects Sections to include: Inclusion Enrollment Report; Protection of Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women and Minorities; Inclusion of Children; Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH instructions for each subcomponent, provide required safety/protection information, and supply enrollment/representation tables as required by the FOA and NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals section
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals — include the required section on use of vertebrate animals in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the full details required by NIH (rationale, veterinary care, procedures to minimize pain/suffering, etc.) as specified in the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide and FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Select Agent Research: A full discussion on the use of Select Agents should appear in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs must describe the biocontainment resources available at all performance sites and follow NIH and institutional policies for select agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/Contractual Arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Consortium/Contractual Arrangements (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the roles, responsibilities, and budgets for consortium organizations; include letters of support or commitment as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should document institutional or collaborator commitments, core facility access, or other resources; ensure they align with the statements made in Facilities & Other Resources and the Budget/Consortium sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Resource Sharing Plan(s) as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plans for sharing data, model organisms, genomic data, software, and other resources per NIH policy and FOA-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available institutional proposal development resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Resources: R-Series Grants Tip Sheet and the Proposal Development team provide formatting requirements, templates, sample proposals, and tips for writing the Research Plan for R01, R15, and R21 grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Proposal Development team for grant writing and editing support and to request assistance or templates (contact information provided).
